papers.title: Recurrent femoral stem fractures in Dorr A femurs: Lessons learned and a call for alternative strategies.
papers.abstract: We report a unique case of bilateral femoral stem fractures in a patient with Dorr A femoral morphology, underscoring the need for a critical reassessment of implant selection strategies. The initial failure involved a cemented revision stem placed using the cement-within-cement technique combined with an extended trochanteric osteotomy (ETO). A second revision was subsequently performed using a cortical window osteotomy and a distally fixed uncemented stem, which resulted in successful recovery. A similar approach was used to treat a subsequent contralateral stem fracture, also with favorable outcomes. This case emphasizes three key considerations: First, that standard-length cemented stems may lead to oversizing and increased stress concentration in Dorr A femurs with narrow canals; second, that ETO may compromise femoral integrity and contribute to implant failure; and third, that cortical window osteotomy enables safer implant removal and reimplantation. Based on these findings, we advocate for an individualized approach to implant selection that may include cemented short stems, uncemented short stems, or modular solutions depending on femoral anatomy and patient-specific factors, and we encourage further investigation into optimal fixation strategies for patients with Dorr A femoral morphology.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文报告了Dorr A型股骨柄的临床断裂案例，但未涉及任何生物力学建模、有限元分析或增材制造设计。
llm.why_not_core: This is a clinical case report without biomechanical modeling, FEA, implant design optimization, or additive manufacturing, which are core to the user's directions.

summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析双侧股骨柄断裂病例的临床处理与术后结果。
summary_zh.result: 标准长度骨水泥柄可能导致应力集中，皮质窗截骨有助于安全翻修。

summary_en.motivation: This case report highlights recurrent femoral stem fractures in Dorr A femurs, aiming to prompt a critical reassessment of implant selection strategies for this morphology.
summary_en.method: The authors detail the clinical management of bilateral stem fractures using cement-within-cement technique and extended trochanteric osteotomy, followed by cortical window osteotomy and distally fixed uncemented stems.
summary_en.result: Oversizing of standard-length cemented stems and extended trochanteric osteotomy may compromise femoral integrity, while cortical window osteotomy facilitates safer revision with favorable outcomes.
summary_en.validation: The findings are based on two clinical cases without biomechanical or experimental validation.
